disagreements.topic: Why agent 5's DCF ($5.19 split / $4.25 single) sits $3-7 above the rest (-$2.27 to $1.63)
disagreements.positions: Agent 5: Tydal LC years at 7.0% and years 6-10 at 9.5%; A202 +$475M; A201 +$786M; refresh cohorts at 80% of today's revenue per $ of capex; corporate cost only -$805M (G&A assumed inside the CoinShares cash cost, R&D cut from ~$110M to $60M after the halving); mining terminal growth +1.5%; a 65/35 weighting of rising BTC ($115-125k in 2029-31) vs flat $85k. Agents 1, 2 and 4: corporate cost $214-220M/yr (-$1.5B to -$2.2B PV), mining terminal -3%/yr, A202 between -$144M and +$106M.
disagreements.resolution: Five of agent 5's choices make it the outlier, and one goes the other way. (1) The 7.0% rate is below the only market evidence. TeraWulf's 7.75% notes were fully covered by a Google backstop and priced on 2025-10-16, when the 5-year Treasury was ~3.6%. At today's 5.09% 5Y / 5.29% 10Y that is ~9%, and Tydal's LCs are still 'anticipated' and the halls are unbuilt. Re-anchoring to 9.0%/11.0% costs -$0.34. (2) The refresh cycles are positive-NPV by construction. At NPV-zero (its own 60% sensitivity) the cost is -$1.72. Most of A202's $475M is that refresh chain: its first cohort nets to about zero. (3) The A202 facility fee is Bitdeer's fixed obligation but is discounted at the 12.5% WACC, not ~10%: -$0.20. (4) +1.5% mining terminal growth ignores the 2032 and 2036 halvings; at -3% (agents 1, 2, 4) the rising path loses -$0.68. (5) Cutting R&D to $60M against $112M/yr actual (H1-26 $56.3M) is unsupported; at ~$90M the cost is -$0.70. Against these, CoinShares' cash cost, which agent 5 uses, includes allocated net interest ($9,751 of the $61,051/BTC ex-tax in Q2-26). An FCFF that also deducts net debt therefore counts interest twice, which is conservative: about +$2.75 on the rising path and +$1.5 on the flat path. G&A does sit inside the CoinShares figure (allocated by self-mining revenue share), so on that point agent 5 is right. The BTC weighting rests on Polymarket odds; with BTC at $86.9k and no checked edge I weight 50/50. Corrected: rising $5.77, flat $1.01, central $3.39 at 50/50 ($4.10 at 65/35). Single-rate ~$2.99.
disagreements.evidence: Treasury daily par yield curve CSV (9/30/2026 10Y 5.29%, 5Y 5.09%; Oct-2025 10Y ~4.05%); TeraWulf 8-K/press 2025-10-16 ($3.2B 7.75% due 2030, $3.2B Google backstop covers debt); CoinShares Bitcoin Mining Report Q2-2026 (cash cost = cost of revenue ex-D&A + SG&A ex-SBC + net interest + tax, allocated; Bitdeer $61,051 ex-tax, interest $9,751, R&D $11.3k excluded); Bitdeer H1-26 FS 6-K Ex.99.1 (G&A $58.9M, R&D $56.3M, selling $5.1M, SBC $13.5M).

disagreements.topic: Contract discount rates and their anchors
disagreements.positions: LC-backed Tydal rent: agent 1 8.5% (on the 28% LC share of in-term cash), agent 2 8.75%, agent 3 8.0%, agent 4 9.0%, agent 5 7.0%. Volta-only in-term rent: 11.0 / 10.5 / 10.5 / 11.0 / 9.5%. GPU offtakes: 10.5-12%. All five keep Tydal years 11-16 (no-fee walk), tails, pipeline and terminal at WACC.
disagreements.resolution: No contract-level debt is priced (sites.json contracts_credit), so the anchor is HPC project debt with a backstop: TeraWulf 7.75% (Oct-2025) and Cipher 7.125% (Nov-2025), ~3.4-4.1pp over Treasuries at the time. Re-based to today's curve that is ~8.5-9.2%. Agents 1, 2 and 4 are sound. Agent 3's 8.0% adds only 25bp to the old coupon and skips the ~1.2pp rise in Treasuries, so it should be ~9% (-$0.10). Agent 5's 7.0%/9.5% are unsound (-$0.34). Every agent applies the contract rate only inside the firm term. A201 'commitments' get contract rates at 80-95% probability although the release does not say they are executed. I accept this because the probability is applied separately, but it is the weakest use of a contract rate.
disagreements.evidence: Treasury yield CSV; TeraWulf pricing release 2025-10-16; agent discounting blocks.

disagreements.positions: Agents 1-4 switched to 128 systems (Q2 PR plan). Agent 5 kept 133, citing the Aug-2026 6-K.
disagreements.resolution: Agent 5 is right. The Aug-2026 update 6-K says Bitdeer 'advanced hardware readiness for its A201 facility by procuring 133 racks of GB300'. The inventory's 128-vs->100 conflict misses this. Agents 1-4 understate A201 capex by ~$20-23M (~-$0.07-0.08/sh).

disagreements.positions: All five now treat Bitdeer as the customer paying a 10-yr facility fee, with no offtake. Values: agent 1 +$5M, agent 2 -$144M, agent 3 +$64M, agent 4 +$106M, agent 5 +$475M.
disagreements.resolution: Direction re-verified: the 9/14 release says 'No offtake commitments have been entered into with respect to A201 or A202 capacity' and that Bitdeer 'expects the per-MW economics of A202 to be broadly consistent with those of A102'. The fee is undisclosed; agents' estimates run $65-98M/yr. Agent 2 (12%) and agent 5 (12.5%) discount this fixed obligation at WACC, which understates it; agents 1/3 (9%) and agent 4 (11%) are right. Once refresh cycles are NPV-zero, A202 is worth roughly -$0.15B to +$0.1B. It is a funding call (~$1.6-1.8B of GPUs) more than a value source.

disagreements.positions: Agents 1/2/4 build mining cost bottom-up and charge $214-220M/yr of corporate cost. Agents 3/5 use the CoinShares cash cost and add only R&D (+$30M overhead for agent 5).
disagreements.resolution: Settled. CoinShares' cash cost includes SG&A ex-SBC allocated by self-mining revenue share, so both approaches avoid double-counting G&A. But CoinShares also includes allocated net interest (~$105M/yr for Bitdeer at Q2 run-rate), so agents 3 and 5 double-count interest against net debt (conservative). Agent 5's R&D cut to $60M is not supported by the $112M/yr run-rate. Agent 3 cuts R&D to $60M as well and also uses +1.5% terminal growth; for agent 3 these roughly offset the interest effect and I leave them unquantified.
disagreements.evidence: CoinShares Q2-2026 mining report methodology; Bitdeer H1-26 FS.

one_month_reasoning: I keep the forecasters' 1-month mean. They agree within 0.025 at every strike, and the window (to 10/31) holds only the mid-October September production update and BTC/financing headlines. Q3 results (~Nov 9-18) fall outside it. BTC rose 2.4% on 10/2 to ~$86.9k, which is noise at a ~30% monthly sigma.
confidence_reason: Primary checks settled five facts that matter: Treasury yields (5.29% 10Y confirmed), the TeraWulf anchor, the CoinShares cost definition (includes G&A and interest), the A201 rack count and A202's lack of offtake. Together they cut agent 5's DCF from $5.19 to ~$3.4 and the corrected fair-value mean to ~$4.9 (agent mean $5.36). The 12-month price is driven mostly by BTC and lease optionality, so I move the ladder only ~3% in strike terms. That is not enough for 'high'.
thesis_break_reason: At ~$5.0-5.3, market cap (~$1.37-1.45B on 273M shares) equals net debt (~$1.40-1.45B). Equity would then be worth about the contracted Tydal + A102 + A201 value at split rates (~$1.5-2.0B, net of capex) and nothing for 80 EH/s of mining or ~3 GW of power. Getting there would most likely take a Volta LC/backstop failure, a refinancing squeeze on the $491M of current BIT loans, A201 commitments not converting with 133 GB300 racks bought, or a deep-discount equity raise. The agents' 4.0-5.4 bracket this level.
key_drivers: BTC/hashprice into the April-2028 halving: mining is still ~65-70% of 2027 revenue. Agent 5's corrected DCF is $5.77 on a rising-BTC path and $1.01 flat, and agent 4's hashprice +/-20% gives +$1.76/-$6.31
On cash flows alone EV ~= net debt. Corrected split-rate DCFs run -$2.34 to $3.39 (mean ~-$0.05) and single-rate -$2.84 to $2.99 (mean ~-$0.50), so splitting the discount rate adds only ~$0.45/sh

Tydal: $233M yr-1 rent from ~2027-04-01. ~$1.3B LCs still 'anticipated'. Worth ~$0.9-1.0B net of capex at a ~9% LC-backed / ~11% Volta-only rate; TeraWulf's backstopped 7.75% notes, re-based to a 5.29% 10Y, anchor ~9%, not 7%

Malaysia GPU cloud: A102 >$800M signed; A201 >70% 'commitments' (>$1.7B / 5 yrs), 133 GB300 racks procured; A202 65.1 MW with no offtake and a 10-yr fee Bitdeer pays. Whether refresh cycles earn above their cost of capital moves agents 1 and 5 by ~$1.5-1.7/sh, more than GPU life does

Corporate cost and the mining cost base: $112M/yr of R&D plus ~$105M of G&A (H1-26 FS). CoinShares' cash cost already holds allocated G&A and ~$9.75k/BTC of interest, so agents using it must neither add G&A nor deduct interest twice

fair_value.reason: Round-4 blends are $6.51 / $3.50 / $4.70 / $4.58 / $7.51 (mean $5.36). Corrections: agent 1 to ~$6.48 (A201 133 racks); agent 2 to ~$3.41 (A202 fee at ~10% not WACC, 133 racks); agent 3 to ~$4.57 (Tydal LC rate 8.0% -> ~9% after re-basing to today's Treasuries, 133 racks); agent 4 to ~$4.54 (133 racks); agent 5 to ~$5.55 (DCF $5.19 -> $3.39: LC/Volta rates 7.0/9.5% -> 9/11%, NPV-zero refresh, A202 fee at ~10%, mining terminal -3% for the 2032 halving, R&D held ~$90M, partly offset by removing CoinShares' allocated interest, BTC paths weighted 50/50; SOTP $8.18 -> ~$4.9 on the same fixes; EV/sales $11.54 kept). Corrected mean ~$4.9, ~54% below the $10.64 spot. The gap is option value on BTC, a second lease and market multiples on powered MW.

summary: In round 4 all five forecasters valued every inventory site once and split discount rates. After my fixes the split-rate DCFs run -$2.34 to $3.39 (mean ~-$0.05) and single-rate -$2.84 to $2.99 (mean ~-$0.50). Agent 5's $5.19 was the outlier: a 7% Tydal rate below the TeraWulf evidence, positive-NPV GPU refresh, an A202 fee at WACC, a mining perpetuity that ignores the 2032 halving and an unsupported R&D cut, partly offset by a real interest double count in the CoinShares cost it uses. Corrected fair value is ~$4.9 against a $10.64 spot. I shade the ladder ~3% lower (P(>=spot) 0.36) with medium confidence; thesis break is $5.0. The stock is a leveraged option on BTC and a second lease, with no checked edge over SPY.
